summary_paragraph: A  woman with a history of neurogenic bladder from a prior gunshot wound, urostomy placement earlier in the year, type II diabetes, and right below-knee amputation was admitted for new-onset pain around her urostomy site and gross hematuria. She had no fever or leukocytosis, and initial urinalysis showed blood and white cells but urine culture revealed fecal contamination rather than true infection. A CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis showed no nephrolithiasis or fluid collection, ruling out stones or abscess. The clinical picture was consistent with urostomy site inflammation. Pain and hematuria resolved during the hospital stay with supportive care, and antibiotics were discontinued. She was discharged home with improved symptoms, instructions for follow-up with primary care and urology, and a plan for ongoing stoma and pain management.
